header: Run with: collector stop, useMaxFPS 0 (maxFPS 120), vsync 0.
Compared with: no earlier comparable round.
notes: **Lua:** the call's own time (debugprofilestop). Below 0.01 ms it is timer noise: no factor.

**Frame:** from the call's start to the next frame, the work WoW defers to drawing included, minus the block's idle frame (each block starts with one). "≈ idle" is within the idle frames' own spread (p95 above median): no factor.

**Engine / backend:** the framework row's Lua time on the stub backend (the engine alone) and the rest (the drawing backend's share). Lua only: the stub draws nothing, so its frame times mean nothing. The stub's empty calls (about 0.1 ms per 1000) count as engine time, so the backend's share reads slightly low.

**Net KB:** Lua heap growth per call with the collector stopped (negative: a call that frees). **Kept KB** (make rows): what stays after a full collection. The Lua heap only: WoW frames' own memory is invisible to every side.
**¹** a single sample (a first opening, a hand make): its frame time is one frame's, not a median.
**Built as players run it:** every round is on the bench profile (release stripping, the bench's dev hooks kept) with the debug addon disabled; bench_save refuses any other.

**Engine / backend, read with care:** the stub run touches less memory, so the engine runs with warmer caches there and the backend's share reads slightly high. Hand-written drawing leaves its text layout to WoW's drawing, so compare the backend with best's frame column, not its Lua column.

**Change:** against the newest earlier comparable round (clean builds); an improvement or a regression is a change of 10% or more (frame changes also beyond the idle spread). Same graphics quality and spot in the world (zone and subzone) only; stand in the same place facing the same way, since the world drawn is in every frame time.
orders: grid small: baseline, typical, framework, framework-itemsRead, framework-naive, framework-engine
grid large: baseline, typical, framework, framework-itemsRead, framework-naive, framework-engine
ticker small: typical, framework, framework-naive, framework-engine, baseline
ticker large: typical, framework, framework-naive, framework-engine, baseline
reading: **One /obench:** a cold block first (the large grid opened on every side while the session is fresh), then the whole plan untracked (one-time costs: fonts, first textures, Blizzard code), then the whole plan measured.
**make (pool warm):** the framework opened again after closing, its frames back from the pools; hand code makes new frames every time. **make (cold)** compares the first opening on every side.
**grid close and open+close:** the framework unmounts and mounts again (the MVP has no hidden attribute); hand code hides and shows ("By hand only"). Not the same operation: no factor.

**framework-naive:** grid and ticker written as code reads without the build's lifting and hoisting: new tables and a new slot function every call. Its rows include lost skipping (a new slot function re-renders the child), not only allocation.
**grid steady:** the grid on screen with nothing changing. "≈ idle" means the CPU pays nothing for drawing it at this frame rate (the GPU may); not that drawing is free on every machine.
**deep, value through 100 levels:** the framework hands the value down as an attribute through every level; hand code sets the one text directly. Intended: it shows what passing attributes costs.

**rows, filter, tooltip, sections:** the framework releases the nodes of what goes away and takes them (from its pools) for what comes back; hand code hides and shows frames it keeps. That difference is in their rows.

**hover:** the bench calls the cells' frames' OnLeave and OnEnter scripts; WoW finding the frame under the cursor (hit testing) is the same on every side and isn't measured. No engine side: the stub draws no frames.
